questions.question: Which tissue is responsible for the size of the roots of plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Apical Meristem**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Apical Meristem** is responsible for the growth and increase in the size of the roots of plants.
 
• The meristematic tissues are regions of actively dividing cells in plants.
 
• Apical Meristem is located at the tips of roots and shoots, contributing to the primary growth of the plant.
 
• It allows the roots to penetrate deeper into the soil, aiding in the absorption of water and nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Meristematic tissues are classified into three types based on their location: **Apical Meristem, Intercalary Meristem, and Lateral Meristem**.
 
• **Apical Meristem** is found at the tips of roots and shoots and is responsible for the vertical growth of the plant.
 
• **Intercalary Meristem** is located at the base of leaves or internodes and helps in the elongation of these parts.
 
• **Lateral Meristem**, such as the vascular cambium and cork cambium, is responsible for the increase in the girth of the plant.
 
• Plant tissues are broadly classified into **meristematic tissues** and **permanent tissues**.
 
• Permanent tissues are further divided into simple tissues (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma) and complex tissues (xylem and phloem).

questions.question: What type of energy is in a stretched rubber band?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Potential energy__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• When you stretch a rubber band, the energy transferred is stored in the form of potential energy.

 
 
• When elastic is stretched, it's loaded with potential energy, when released there is a shift to kinetic energy.
 
• This is especially true if the elastic is transporting another object, such as with a rock being flung from a slingshot.
 
• Potential energy is the energy held by an object because of its position relative to other objects, stresses within itself, its electric charge, or other factors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Muscular energy is the conscious movement of energy along the lines of the body, drawing muscle to bone and connecting limbs to joints as the energy moves ever inward to the body's core.
 
• Mechanical energy is the sum of the kinetic energy, or energy of motion, and the potential energy, or energy stored in a system by reason of the position of its parts.
 
 
• Neglecting friction at the pivot and air resistance, the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of the pendulum, or its mechanical energy, is constant.
 
 
 
• Kinetic energy is a form of energy that an object or a particle has by reason of its motion.
 
 
• Kinetic energy is a property of a moving object or particle and depends not only on its motion but also on its mass.

questions.question: Which of the following is a double-displacement reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Na2SO4 (aq) + BaCl2 (aq) → BaSO4 (s) + 2NaCl (aq)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 4** represents a double-displacement reaction.
 
• In a double-displacement reaction, two compounds exchange ions to form two new compounds.
 
• The reaction **Na2SO4 (aq) + BaCl2 (aq) → BaSO4 (s) + 2NaCl (aq)** involves the exchange of ions between Na2SO4 and BaCl2.
 
• This results in the formation of BaSO4, a solid precipitate, and NaCl, which remains in the aqueous phase.
 
• Such reactions are also known as metathesis reactions and are characterized by the formation of a precipitate, gas, or a weak electrolyte.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Single-displacement reactions** involve one element being displaced from a compound by another element.
 
• Examples of single-displacement reactions include options 1, 2, and 3, where a metal displaces another metal from its compound.
 
• In contrast, **double-displacement reactions** require the exchange of ions between two reacting compounds, as seen in option 4.
 
• Double-displacement reactions are common in precipitation reactions, neutralization reactions, and gas formation reactions.

questions.question: When the force and the displacement are in the same direction, then work done will be:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**positive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When the **force** and **displacement** are in the same direction, the **angle between force and displacement** is **0 degrees**.
 
• The mathematical expression for **work done** is given as: **Work (W) = Force (F) × Displacement (d) × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
• When θ = 0°, the value of **cos(θ) = 1**, so the formula simplifies to: **W = F × d × 1 = F × d.**
 
• Since both force and displacement are in the same direction, their magnitudes are **positive**, leading to a **positive value for work done**.
 
• This signifies that the energy is being **transferred to the object**, causing displacement in the direction of the applied force.
 
• Examples include pushing a box forward or lifting an object upwards, where the displacement occurs in the same direction as the applied force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zero**__

 __
 
• If the angle between force and displacement is **90 degrees**, then the **cos(90°) = 0**, resulting in **zero work done**.
 
• This happens when the force does not contribute to the displacement, such as carrying an object horizontally without vertical displacement.
 
 
 
• **Negative**__
 __
 
• If the force and displacement are in **opposite directions**, the angle θ = 180°, and **cos(180°) = -1**, leading to **negative work done**.
 
• Negative work is observed when a force opposes the motion, such as friction slowing down a moving object.
 
 
 
• **Either Positive or Negative**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect as the work done depends on the **specific relationship** between the force and displacement directions.
 
• It cannot be both positive and negative at the same time; it depends on the angle θ.

 **H = I²Rt**

questions.question: A person observing a passing train hears a shift in whistle frequency. Which principle explains this effect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doppler effect**__.

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Doppler effect** refers to the change in the frequency or wavelength of a wave in relation to an observer who is moving relative to the source of the wave.
 
• In the scenario described in the question, the train is moving, causing the frequency of the sound waves (the whistle) to change as perceived by the observer.
 
• When the train moves towards the observer, the sound waves compress, resulting in a **higher frequency** or pitch. Conversely, when the train moves away from the observer, the sound waves stretch, leading to a **lower frequency** or pitch.
 
• The change in sound frequency is directly proportional to the relative velocity between the observer and the source. This is why the train's whistle appears to change pitch as it approaches and then moves away from the observer.
 
• *Hence, this effect is best explained by the Doppler effect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Doppler Effect:**

 
 
• The Doppler Effect is named after **Christian Doppler**, who proposed it in **1842**. This principle applies to all types of waves, including sound, light, and electromagnetic waves.
 
• **Applications:** The Doppler effect is used in various fields such as **astronomy** (to measure the velocity of stars and galaxies), **medical imaging** (Doppler ultrasound), and **radar technology** (to measure the speed of moving objects).
 
• **Formula:** The observed frequency (f'*) is given by the formula: *f' = f (v + vo) / (v + vs)*, where **f** is the source frequency, **v** is the speed of sound, **vo** is the observer's velocity, and **vs** is the source's velocity.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Sound Refraction:** Refers to the bending of sound waves as they pass through different media with varying densities. It is not related to changes in frequency due to motion.
 
• **Sound Diffraction:** Refers to the bending of sound waves around obstacles or through openings. It has no relation to the change in pitch due to relative motion.
 
• **Resonance:** Refers to the phenomenon where an object vibrates at its natural frequency due to the influence of another vibrating object. It is not related to the change in sound frequency perceived by an observer.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real-life Examples of Doppler Effect:**

 
 
• The change in pitch of a police siren as it approaches and then moves away from an observer.
 
• Astronomers use the Doppler effect to determine if celestial objects are moving towards or away from Earth (redshift and blueshift).
 
• In weather forecasting, Doppler radar is used to measure wind speed and detect storms.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Doppler Effect in Sound:**
 
 
• The effect is more pronounced when the relative speed between the source and observer is high.

questions.question: Which one of the following is an example of chemical change?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Burning of magnesium in air** is a **chemical change**, as it results in the formation of a new substance, magnesium oxide (MgO).
 
• When magnesium burns, it reacts with **oxygen** in the air, producing a bright white flame and forming a completely new compound.
 
• This process involves a **chemical reaction** where magnesium (Mg) combines with oxygen (O₂) to form magnesium oxide (MgO).
 
• The reaction can be represented by the equation: **2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO**.
 
• This is an example of an **exothermic reaction**, as energy is released in the form of heat and light.
 
• A key indicator of a chemical change is the formation of a new substance with different chemical properties, which is evident in this reaction.
 
• Magnesium oxide is a white powder, distinctly different from the original metallic magnesium.
 
• This reaction is also irreversible under normal conditions, further confirming it as a chemical change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Melting of wax**__

 __
 
• **Melting of wax** is a **physical change**, as no new substance is formed during the process.
 
• It involves a change of state from solid to liquid due to the application of heat, but the chemical composition of wax remains the same.
 
• This process is reversible, as the wax can solidify again upon cooling.
 
 
 
• **Heating of iron**__
 __
 
• When iron is merely heated (without reacting with any other substance), it does not undergo a **chemical change**.
 
• The heating process may cause a **temporary expansion** or change in physical state, but the chemical properties of iron remain unchanged.
 
 
 
• **Dissolution of sugar in water**__
 
 
• This is a **physical change**, as the sugar molecules disperse in water but retain their chemical identity.
 
• The process is reversible, as the sugar can be recovered by evaporating the water.

questions.question: Two circles of radius 7 units each, intersect in such a way that the common chord is of length 7 units. What is the common area in square units of the intersection?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **radius (r) = 7** and **chord (L) = 7**, the triangle formed by the center and the chord is **equilateral**.

Central angle (θ) = 60° = π/3 radians.

Common area = 2 × (Area of Sector − Area of Equilateral Triangle)

Area = 2 × [(π × 7² × 60/360) − (√3/4 × 7²)]

Area = 2 × [49π/6 − 49√3/4] = 98(π/6 − √3/4) sq. units.

**∴ The correct answer is 98(π/6 − √3/4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of both circles (r) = 7 units

Length of common chord (AB) = 7 units

**Formula Used:**

Area of Segment = Area of Sector − Area of Triangle

Area of Sector = (θ/360°) × πr²

Area of Equilateral Triangle = (√3/4) × side²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b7de5a966afe80b79794e74617fe9d4345421929e7a5671328e4906471759e2.png] 

⇒ In ▵O₁AB, O₁A = O₁B = 7 (radii) and AB = 7 (given chord).

⇒ Since all sides are equal, ▵O₁AB is an **equilateral triangle**.

⇒ Central angle θ = 60°.

⇒ Area of sector O₁AB = (60/360) × π × 7² = 49π/6.

⇒ Area of ▵O₁AB = (√3/4) × 7² = 49√3/4.

⇒ Area of segment (one side) = Area of sector − Area of triangle = (49π/6) − (49√3/4).

⇒ Total common area = 2 × [49π/6 − 49√3/4].

⇒ Total common area = 98(π/6 − √3/4) sq. units.

**∴ The correct answer is 98(π/6 − √3/4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Circular Segment

The area of a segment of a circle is calculated as A = (1/2) × r² × (θ − sin θ), where θ is in radians.

Common Chord Property

The common chord of two intersecting circles is perpendicular to the line joining their centers and is bisected by it.

Equilateral Triangle Area

For a triangle with side 'a', Area = (√3/4) × a² and the internal angles are all 60°.</p

questions.question: A man walking at the speed of 5 km/h covers a certain distance in 3 hours 45 minutes. If he covers the same distance by a cycle in 2 hours 10 minutes, then the speed of the cycle in km/h is:

For a constant distance, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**.

Time 1 (Walk) = 3 h 45 min = 225 min | Time 2 (Cycle) = 2 h 10 min = 130 min

Time Ratio (Walk : Cycle) = 225 : 130 = 45 : 26

Speed Ratio (Walk : Cycle) = 26 : 45

If 26 units = 5 km/h, then 45 units = (5 ÷ 26) × 45 = 225/26 = 8 17/26 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 8(17)/(26) km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time = 5 × (15/4) = 75/4 km

⇒ Cycling time = 2 + 10/60 = 2 + 1/6 = 13/6 hours

⇒ Cycling Speed = Distance ÷ Cycling time = (75/4) ÷ (13/6)

⇒ Cycling Speed = (75/4) × (6/13) = (75 × 3) / (2 × 13) = 225/26

⇒ Cycling Speed = 8 17/26 km/h

Speed-Time Relation

When distance is constant, Speed₁ × Time₁ = Speed₂ × Time₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

Average Speed

For the same distance covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x + y).</p

questions.question: If ΔABC and ΔPQR are similar. AB = 8 cm, PQ = 12 cm, QR = 18 cm and RP = 24 cm, then the perimeter of ΔABC is _________ cm.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Perimeter of ΔPQR = PQ + QR + RP = 12 + 18 + 24 = 54 cm

Ratio of corresponding sides = AB / PQ = 8 / 12 = 2 / 3

Perimeter of ΔABC = 54 × (2 / 3) = 36 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

AB = 8 cm

PQ = 12 cm

QR = 18 cm

RP = 24 cm

ΔABC ~ ΔPQR

**Formula Used:**

For two similar triangles, the ratio of their perimeters is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides:

Perimeter(ΔABC) / Perimeter(ΔPQR) = AB / PQ = BC / QR = CA / RP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c915b7e6c39814636414cedc3eaca66decb41a196ad73642c855739f7673ffdb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter of ΔPQR = PQ + QR + RP

⇒ Perimeter of ΔPQR = 12 + 18 + 24 = 54 cm

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) / Perimeter(ΔPQR) = AB / PQ

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) / 54 = 8 / 12

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) / 54 = 2 / 3

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) = 54 × (2 / 3)

⇒ Perimeter(ΔABC) = 18 × 2 = 36 cm

**Option Analysis:**

**Option (1) 36:** This is the correct perimeter of ΔABC as calculated above.

**Option (2) 54:** This is the perimeter of ΔPQR, not ΔABC.

**Option (3) 27:** This value is incorrect because the ratio of perimeters must be 2:3, which gives 36 cm, not 27 cm.

**Option (4) 42:** This value is incorrect because it does not satisfy the similarity ratio of 2:3 with the perimeter of ΔPQR (54 cm).

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their corresponding sides is equal to the ratio of their perimeters, altitudes, medians, and angle bisectors.

Area Ratio Theorem

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔPQR) = (AB / PQ)².

Criteria for Similarity

Two triangles are similar if they satisfy any of the following criteria: Angle-Angle (AA), Side-Angle-Side (SAS), or Side-Side-Side (SSS).</p

questions.question: One company is offering a 25% discount on a particular product. Anurag visited a store. He was trying to find a deal that would allow him to save at least Rs. 390. How many minimum items should he purchase if each item costs Rs. 340?

questions.question: When the integer n is divided by 18, the quotient is x and the remainder is 6, When the integer n is divided by 25, the quotient is y and the remainder is 15. Which of the following is true?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Express **n** in terms of both **quotients** and **remainders**.

n = 18x + 6 and n = 25y + 15.

Equating both: 18x + 6 = 25y + 15.

Rearranging: 18x − 25y = 15 − 6 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 18x − 25y = 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**n** divided by **18** gives **quotient x** and **remainder 6**.

**n** divided by **25** gives **quotient y** and **remainder 15**.

**Formula Used:**

**Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6820b9482e94e44ea90ff1e9bb3c37add58e65f6cbad7b9184c9d1fc8471a2fa.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Case 1: n = 18 × x + 6

⇒ Case 2: n = 25 × y + 15

⇒ Equating n: 18x + 6 = 25y + 15

⇒ 18x − 25y = 15 − 6

⇒ 18x − 25y = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 18x − 25y = 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Euclid's Division Lemma

For any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, where 0 ≤ r < b.

Linear Diophantine Equation

Equations of the form ax + by = c are solvable if the greatest common divisor (GCD) of a and b divides c.

Verification Rule

Always ensure the remainder is smaller than the divisor. If n = dq + r, then r must be in the range [0, d−1].</p

questions.question: Find the lowest positive value of (c – b) such that the 7-digit number 1738b9c is divisible by 12.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a number to be divisible by 12, it must be divisible by both 3 and 4.

For divisibility by 4, the last two digits 9c must be divisible by 4 ⇒ c = 2 or c = 6.

For divisibility by 3, the sum of all digits (28 + b + c) must be a multiple of 3.

If c = 6, the digit sum is 34 + b. For this to be a multiple of 3, b can be 2, 5, or 8.

To find the lowest positive value of (c − b), we take c = 6 and b = 5 ⇒ 6 − 5 = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The 7-digit number 1738b9c is completely divisible by 12.

**Concept Used:**

A number is divisible by 12 if it is divisible by both 3 (sum of digits is a multiple of 3) and 4 (last two digits form a multiple of 4).

**Calculation:**

⇒ Divisibility by 4: The number formed by the last two digits is 9c.

⇒ The only numbers in the 90s divisible by 4 are 92 and 96. Thus, c = 2 or c = 6.

⇒ Divisibility by 3: The sum of digits = 1 + 7 + 3 + 8 + b + 9 + c = 28 + b + c must be divisible by 3.

⇒ Case 1: If c = 2, the sum = 30 + b. For the sum to be completely divisible by 3, b can be 0, 3, 6, or 9.

⇒ We need a positive value for (c − b), so c must be greater than b. Thus, b = 0 ⇒ (c − b) = 2 − 0 = 2.

⇒ Case 2: If c = 6, the sum = 34 + b. For the sum to be completely divisible by 3, b can be 2, 5, or 8.

⇒ For a positive value of (c − b), b can be 2 or 5.

⇒ If b = 2, (c − b) = 6 − 2 = 4.

⇒ If b = 5, (c − b) = 6 − 5 = 1.

⇒ Comparing all valid positive outcomes (2, 4, and 1), the lowest possible positive value is 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is completely divisible by 3 or 9 respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4, and divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: An iron box with external dimensions 60 cm, 40 cm, and 20 cm is made of 1 cm thick sheet. If 1 cm³ of iron weighs 50 gm, the weight of the empty box is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**External Volume** = 60 × 40 × 20 = 48,000 cm³

**Internal dimensions** (subtracting 2 cm from each): 58, 38, 18

**Internal Volume** = 58 × 38 × 18 = 39,672 cm³

**Volume of Iron** = 48,000 − 39,672 = 8,328 cm³

**Weight** = 8,328 × 50 gm = 416,400 gm = 416.40 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 416.40 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** External Length (L) = 60 cm, Breadth (B) = 40 cm, Height (H) = 20 cm. Thickness (t) = 1 cm. Density = 50 gm/cm³.

**Formula:** Volume of material = External Volume − Internal Volume

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/06079ee345ae6dd077aacd1d508552180d83c307a96317163fce2990bc7d5210.png] 

⇒ **External Volume** = 60 × 40 × 20 = 48,000 cm³

⇒ **Internal Length (l)** = 60 − (2 × 1) = 58 cm

⇒ **Internal Breadth (b)** = 40 − (2 × 1) = 38 cm

⇒ **Internal Height (h)** = 20 − (2 × 1) = 18 cm

⇒ **Internal Volume** = 58 × 38 × 18 = 39,672 cm³

⇒ **Volume of Iron** = 48,000 − 39,672 = 8,328 cm³

⇒ **Weight in gm** = 8,328 × 50 = 416,400 gm

⇒ **Weight in kg** = 416,400 ÷ 1,000 = 416.40 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 416.40 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cuboid

The volume of a **cuboid** is calculated as Length × Breadth × Height.

Hollow Cuboid Dimensions

For a **hollow box** with thickness 't', the internal dimension is (External Dimension − 2t).

Weight and Density

**Weight** = Volume × Density. Always ensure units are consistent (1 kg = 1000 gm).</p

questions.question: How much water should be added to 60 liters of milk at 1 (1)/(2) liters a rupee so as to have a mixture worth 1 (7)/(8) liters a rupee?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **quantity per rupee** to **price per liter**.

**CP of Milk** = 1 ÷ (3/2) = ₹2/3 per liter.

**CP of Water** = ₹0 per liter.

**Mean Price** = 1 ÷ (15/8) = ₹8/15 per liter.

Using **Alligation**: Ratio of Milk to Water = (8/15 − 0) : (2/3 − 8/15) = 8/15 : 2/15 = 4 : 1.

If 4 units = 60 liters, then 1 unit = 15 liters.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 liters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial quantity of **milk** = 60 liters

Rate of milk = 1.5 liters per rupee ⇒ Price = ₹1/1.5 = ₹2/3 per liter

Rate of mixture = 1.875 liters per rupee ⇒ Price = ₹1/1.875 = ₹8/15 per liter

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40a2ba112d5e170893558edbb8e67ff7c13624c606cea12d4807cb013d90cea0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the quantity of **water** added be 'x' liters.

⇒ Total quantity of mixture = (60 + x) liters.

⇒ Cost of milk + Cost of water = Cost of mixture

⇒ 60 × (2/3) + x × 0 = (60 + x) × (8/15)

⇒ 40 = (60 + x) × 8/15

⇒ 40 × 15 = 480 + 8x

⇒ 600 = 480 + 8x

⇒ 8x = 120

⇒ x = 15 liters

**∴ The correct answer is 15 liters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Rule

It states that (Quantity of cheaper / Quantity of dearer) = (Price of dearer − Mean Price) / (Mean Price − Price of cheaper).

Cost of Water

In problems involving **milk and water**, the cost price of water is always assumed to be **zero** unless specified otherwise.

Unit Consistency

Always ensure all values (CP of cheaper, CP of dearer, and Mean Price) are in the **same units** (e.g., ₹ per liter) before applying the alligation rule.

questions.question: In how many years will the simple interest on a sum of money be equal to the principal at the rate of 2(6)/(7) % per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **Simple Interest** equals **Principal**, the product of **Rate** and **Time** must be 100%.

**Rate (R)** = 2 6/7% = 20/7% per annum.

**Time (T)** = 100 ÷ R = 100 ÷ (20/7)

⇒ T = 100 × 7 ÷ 20 = 5 × 7 = 35 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf8decd65849b930d27ecdefc77c8bf16f389b1fb11d91166f1b0fe977281b1f.png] 

**Given:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = **Principal (P)**

**Rate (R)** = 2 6/7% = (2 × 7 + 6)/7 % = 20/7 % per annum.

**Formula Used:**

**SI** = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ P = (P × (20/7) × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 1 = (20 × T) ÷ (7 × 100)

⇒ 1 = (20 × T) ÷ 700

⇒ 700 = 20 × T

⇒ T = 700 ÷ 20

⇒ T = 35 **years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Concept

Interest calculated only on the initial principal amount throughout the entire period: **SI = (P×R×T)/100**.

Total Amount

The final value after adding interest to the principal: **A = P + SI = P[1 + (R×T)/100]**.

Interest as a Fraction

If **SI** is 1/n of the **Principal**, then the time period **T** can be directly calculated as **100 / (n×R)**.</p

questions.question: Four cubes each of volume 216 cubic cm are joined end to end to form a new solid. The surface area of the new solid is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Side of each cube = √[3]{216} = 6 cm.

Area of one face = 6 × 6 = 36 sq cm.

Total faces in 4 cubes = 4 × 6 = 24 faces.

When 4 cubes are joined, 3 junctions are formed, hiding 3 × 2 = 6 faces.

Remaining visible faces = 24 − 6 = 18 faces.

Total surface area = 18 × 36 = 648 sq cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 648 sq cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of each cube = 216 cm³

Number of cubes = 4

**Formula:**

Side of cube (a) = (Volume)¹/³

Surface area of cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb2b8808275466f679d872530c2d660e264ffaf0409a13d8b3fedf2d43183f7b.png] 

⇒ Side of each cube (a) = √[3]{216} = 6 cm

⇒ When joined end-to-end, only the length changes.

⇒ Length (l) = 4 × 6 = 24 cm

⇒ Breadth (b) = 6 cm

⇒ Height (h) = 6 cm

⇒ Surface Area = 2 × (24×6 + 6×6 + 6×24)

⇒ Surface Area = 2 × (144 + 36 + 144)

⇒ Surface Area = 2 × 324 = 648 sq cm

**∴ The correct answer is 648 sq cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of a Cube

The total surface area of a single cube with side 'a' is 6a².

Volume of a Cuboid

The amount of space occupied by a cuboid is given by Length × Breadth × Height (l × b × h).

Lateral Surface Area

For a cuboid, the area of the four side walls is 2h(l + b).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed in a cuboid has length √(l² + b² + h²).</p

questions.question: What is the value of (1)/(sin⁴(90^circ - 2alpha)) + (1)/(cos²(90^circ - 2alpha) - 1) ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put **α = 15°**, so **2α = 30°**.

Expression: 1/sin⁴(90°−30°) + 1/(cos²(90°−30°) − 1) = 1/sin⁴60° + 1/(cos²60° − 1).

⇒ 1/(√3/2)⁴ + 1/((1/2)² − 1) = 16/9 + 1/(1/4 − 1) = 16/9 − 4/3 = 4/9.

Check options: Option (4) sec²30° × tan²30° = (2/√3)² × (1/√3)² = 4/3 × 1/3 = 4/9.

**∴ The correct answer is sec² 2α tan² 2α.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d46ed134d6b92dc03d2d1f60ad6f3d2c3a6de81eb670865d74fc54b2482c06ce.png] 

**Given:** Expression = 1/sin⁴(90° − 2α) + 1/(cos²(90° − 2α) − 1)

**Formulas Used:** sin(90°−θ) = cosθ; cos(90°−θ) = sinθ; 1−sin²θ = cos²θ

⇒ Expression = 1/cos⁴ 2α + 1/(sin² 2α − 1)

⇒ Expression = 1/cos⁴ 2α − 1/(1 − sin² 2α)

⇒ Expression = 1/cos⁴ 2α − 1/cos² 2α

⇒ Expression = (1 − cos² 2α) / cos⁴ 2α

⇒ Expression = sin² 2α / cos⁴ 2α = (sin² 2α / cos² 2α) × (1 / cos² 2α)

⇒ Expression = tan² 2α × sec² 2α

**∴ The correct answer is sec² 2α tan² 2α.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Rules

Trigonometric ratios change to their co-functions when the angle is (90° − θ): sin ↔ cos, tan ↔ cot, sec ↔ cosec.

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.</p

questions.question: From the salary of a software engineer, if 15% is used as house rent, 25% of the remaining is spent on household items, 25% of the remaining as income tax, and 15% of the remaining on clothing, then he is left with Rs. 10,404. Find his total salary.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **total salary** be 100%.

Remaining salary after all deductions ⇒ 100 × (85/100) × (75/100) × (75/100) × (85/100) = 10,404

Total Salary = 10,404 × (100/85) × (100/75) × (100/75) × (100/85)

Total Salary = 10,404 × (20/17) × (4/3) × (4/3) × (20/17) = 25,600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 25,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1bdc0e12629f1ae29dd43681f8df3e4984288b89aefd7574b15bb10b9a5a06a9.png] 

**Given:**

House Rent = 15% | Household = 25% (Remaining) | Tax = 25% (Remaining) | Clothing = 15% (Remaining)

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (100 − r₁)/100 × (100 − r₂)/100 ...

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let total salary be **S**.

⇒ S × (1 − 0.15) × (1 − 0.25) × (1 − 0.25) × (1 − 0.15) = 10,404

⇒ S × (0.85) × (0.75) × (0.75) × (0.85) = 10,404

⇒ S × (17/20) × (3/4) × (3/4) × (17/20) = 10,404

⇒ S × (26,01/64,00) = 10,404

⇒ S = (10,404 × 6400) ÷ 2601

⇒ S = 4 × 6400 = 25,600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 25,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When values are deducted from the **remaining balance**, we use the multiplying factor (100 − r)/100 for each step.

Base Change Rule

If expenses are given as a % of the **total**, they are simply added; if given as a % of **remaining**, they are multiplied.</p

questions.question: A dozen pairs of gloves of Rs. 180 are available at a discount of 10%. How many pairs of gloves can be bought for Rs. 54?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Discounted Price** of 12 pairs = 180 − (10% of 180) = 180 − 18 = 162.

**Price per pair** = 162 ÷ 12 = 13.5.

**Number of pairs** for Rs. 54 = 54 ÷ 13.5 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 pairs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Marked Price (MP)** of 12 pairs = Rs. 180, **Discount** = 10%, **Total Amount** = Rs. 54.
Formulas: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Quantity = Total Amount ÷ SP per unit.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be5936b74cc1ac55468d55716b728a7ea1e2aaecb6e578a769da96059e7e8fdb.png] 
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** for 12 pairs = 180 × (90 ÷ 100) = Rs. 162.
⇒ Cost of **1 pair** of gloves = 162 ÷ 12 = Rs. 13.5.
⇒ Pairs bought for Rs. 54 = 54 ÷ 13.5.
⇒ Pairs = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 pairs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price** is the price printed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on the MP to find the **Selling Price**.

Unitary Method

Finding the value of a single unit first (price per pair) helps in calculating the quantity for any given total amount.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates A and B, A got 33% of total votes casted and still lost by 55,522 votes. Find the total number of votes got by B.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let the **total votes** be 100%.

**Candidate A** got 33%, so **Candidate B** got (100 − 33) = 67%.

Difference in votes = 67% − 33% = 34%.

Given 34% → 55,522 votes.

Votes of **Candidate B** (67%) = (55,522 ÷ 34) × 67 = 1,633 × 67 = 1,09,411.

**∴ The correct answer is 1,09,411 votes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62e4a09a379d0d35c2c52b9e649c0497771ed6a7cc521e3debba43192f9f89e5.png] 

**Given:**

Votes of **Candidate A** = 33% of total.

**Victory Margin** (Loss margin for A) = 55,522 votes.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Total Votes** = V

⇒ Votes of B = V − 0.33V = 0.67V

⇒ Difference = Votes of B − Votes of A

⇒ 55,522 = 0.67V − 0.33V

⇒ 55,522 = 0.34V

⇒ V = 55,522 ÷ 0.34 = 1,63,300

⇒ Votes of B = 0.67 × 1,63,300

⇒ Votes of B = 1,09,411

**∴ The correct answer is 1,09,411 votes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Percentage change is calculated as (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100.

Valid and Invalid Votes

Total Casted Votes = Valid Votes + Invalid Votes. Winning/Losing margins are usually calculated on valid votes unless specified.

Two Candidate Election Rule

In a two-way contest, if one candidate gets x%, the other must get (100 − x)% of the total votes.</p

questions.question: Mithila covers 50 km by bus in 90 minutes. After deboarding the bus, she takes rest for 15 minutes and covers another 30 km by a taxi in 35 minutes. Find the average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Distance** = 50 + 30 = 80 km

**Total Time** (including rest) = 90 + 15 + 35 = 140 minutes

**Total Time in hours** = 140 ÷ 60 = 7/3 hours

**Average Speed** = 80 ÷ (7/3) = 240/7 = 34(2/7) km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 34(2/7) km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f3f6df9033f049655ad95e72d4ea1cf199506c02d37b6922b764fbfba4aebbcc.png] 

**Given:**

Distance₁ = 50 km, Time₁ = 90 min

Rest Time = 15 min

Distance₂ = 30 km, Time₂ = 35 min

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 50 km + 30 km = 80 km

⇒ Total Time = 90 + 15 + 35 = 140 minutes

⇒ Conversion to hours: 140/60 hours = 7/3 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 80 ÷ (7/3)

⇒ Average Speed = (80 × 3) ÷ 7 = 240/7

⇒ Average Speed = 34(2/7) km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 34(2/7) km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed with Rest

When rest time is included in the journey, it must be added to the total time taken to find the overall average speed for the whole journey.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert time from minutes to hours, divide by 60.

Special Case: Equal Distances

If a person covers two equal distances at speeds V₁ and V₂, the average speed = (2 × V₁ × V₂) ÷ (V₁ + V₂).</p

questions.question: The sum of the five consecutive even numbers is 2720. The sum of the third and fifth numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any **odd number** of terms in an **Arithmetic Progression** (like consecutive even numbers), the **Average** is always the **Middle term**.

**Average** (3rd number) = Total Sum ÷ Number of terms = 2720 ÷ 5 = 544

Since the numbers are **consecutive even**, the common difference is 2.

5th number = 3rd number + (2 × 2) = 544 + 4 = 548

Required Sum = 3rd number + 5th number = 544 + 548 = 1092

**∴ The correct answer is 1092.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of 5 consecutive even numbers = 2720.

questions.question: There are 12 workers in an office and the average age of all the workers is 35 (1)/(2) years. A new worker joins the office, the average becomes 37 years. The current age of the newly joined worker is:

Age of **new worker** = New Average + (Initial Number of Workers × Increase in Average).

Age = 37 + (12 × 1.5) = 37 + 18 = 55 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 55 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Total age of 12 workers = 12 × 35.5 = 426 years.

⇒ Total age of 13 workers (after 1 joins) = 13 × 37 = 481 years.

⇒ Current age of **newly joined worker** = Total age of 13 workers − Total age of 12 workers

Effect of Exclusion

questions.question: The edges of a rectangular box are in the ratio of 3 ∶ 5 ∶ 8, and its surface area is 632 cm². What will be the volume of the box?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **edges** = 3 : 5 : 8

Ratio of **surface area** = 2 × (3×5 + 5×8 + 8×3) = 2 × (15 + 40 + 24) = 158 units²

Given area 158 units² = 632 cm² ⇒ 1 unit² = 4 cm² ⇒ 1 unit = 2 cm

Actual **edges** are (3×2), (5×2), (8×2) = 6 cm, 10 cm, 16 cm

**Volume** = 6 × 10 × 16 = 960 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 960 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of edges of the **rectangular box** = 3 : 5 : 8

Total **Surface Area** (TSA) = 632 cm²

**Formula Used:**

TSA of a cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

Volume of a cuboid = l × b × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/92deae9bacca405a98e7e5b824a2e2cf1e409a71a30d779c0654e07116573820.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the length (l), breadth (b), and height (h) be 3x, 5x, and 8x respectively.

⇒ 2(3x × 5x + 5x × 8x + 8x × 3x) = 632

⇒ 2(15x² + 40x² + 24x²) = 632

⇒ 2(79x²) = 632

⇒ 158x² = 632

⇒ x² = 632 ÷ 158 = 4

⇒ x = √4 = 2

⇒ Dimensions: l = 3×2 = 6 cm, b = 5×2 = 10 cm, h = 8×2 = 16 cm

⇒ **Volume** = 6 × 10 × 16 = 960 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 960 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total area of all six faces of the cuboid, calculated as 2(lb + bh + hl).

Volume of a Cuboid

The space occupied by the box, calculated by the product of its three dimensions: l × b × h.

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed inside the box, given by √(l² + b² + h²).

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The area of the four vertical walls of the box, calculated as 2h(l + b).</p

questions.question: 10 years ago, a man's age was 5 times of his son's age. 2 years hence, twice his age will be equal to 4 times the age of his son. What is the present age (in years) of the son?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio (Man : Son) 10 years ago = 5 : 1 (Difference = 4 units)

Ratio (Man : Son) 2 years hence = 4 : 2 = 2 : 1 (Difference = 1 unit)

Make difference equal: Multiply (2 : 1) by 4 ⇒ New Ratio = 8 : 4

Gap in Son's ratio units = 4 − 1 = 3 units. Total time gap = 10 + 2 = 12 years.

3 units = 12 years ⇒ 1 unit = 4 years.

Son's age 10 years ago = 1 unit = 4 years ⇒ Present age = 4 + 10 = 14 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the present age of the man be M and the son be S.

10 years ago: (M − 10) = 5 × (S − 10)

2 years hence: 2 × (M + 2) = 4 × (S + 2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43f90f63387b96769133d990bb29bf4f23b0137d5d491dae2d2e74cad6675d4f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ M − 10 = 5S − 50

⇒ M = 5S − 40 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ 2(M + 2) = 4(S + 2)

⇒ M + 2 = 2(S + 2)

⇒ M + 2 = 2S + 4

⇒ M = 2S + 2 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ 5S − 40 = 2S + 2

⇒ 3S = 42

⇒ S = 42 ÷ 3

⇒ S = 14 years

**∴ The correct answer is 14 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains constant throughout their lives, regardless of how many years pass.

Sum of Ages Change

If the sum of ages of N people is X today, then after Y years, the new sum will be X + (N × Y).

Ratio Balancing Method

To solve age problems using ratios, always ensure the difference between the ratio parts of two individuals is made equal across different time periods.</p

questions.question: A and B can do a work in 10 days and 40 days, respectively. How long will it take together to complete the work?

Use the direct formula for two people working together: **Time = (X × Y) ÷ (X + Y)**.

Here X = 10 days and Y = 40 days.

Combined Time = (10 × 40) ÷ (10 + 40) = 400 ÷ 50 = 8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:** **Total Work** = LCM of individual days; **Efficiency** = Total Work ÷ Days.

⇒ **Total Efficiency** of (A + B) = 4 + 1 = 5 units/day.

⇒ **Time taken** together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

Work and Efficiency Relation

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to the **Time** taken to complete a work. If the ratio of time is a:b, the ratio of efficiency is b:a.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept is identical to **Time and Work**, where an inlet pipe does positive work and a leakage/outlet pipe does negative work.

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the **Work Done** by the individuals, which is usually the ratio of their **Efficiencies** if they work for the same duration.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the ten indicators used in calculating the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Internet connectivity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is calculated using ten indicators across three broad dimensions: **health, education, and standard of living**.
 
• The indicators under the health dimension include **nutrition** and **child mortality**.
 
• Under the education dimension, the indicators used are **years of schooling** and **school attendance**.
 
• The standard of living dimension includes indicators such as **access to electricity**, drinking water, sanitation, cooking fuel, housing, and asset ownership.
 
• **Internet connectivity** is not one of the indicators used in calculating the MPI, as it focuses on basic needs and capabilities rather than technological access.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• Developed by the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• Aims to provide a more comprehensive measure of poverty beyond just income levels.
 
• It captures the overlapping deprivations individuals or households face across multiple dimensions.
 
 
 
• **Dimensions and Indicators:**
 
 
• Health: Nutrition, Child Mortality.
 
• Education: Years of Schooling, School Attendance.
 
• Standard of Living: Cooking Fuel, Sanitation, Drinking Water, Electricity, Housing, Assets.
 
 
 
• **Global MPI Reports:**
 
 
• The MPI is included in the **Human Development Reports** released annually by the UNDP.
 
• It provides valuable insights into poverty trends and is used for policymaking and international comparisons.
 
 
 
• **Focus on Basic Needs:**
 
 
• The MPI emphasizes fundamental human needs such as health, education, and basic living standards.
 
• Technological access, including internet connectivity, is not included as it is not considered a core indicator of poverty reduction.

• The 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD) Convention is scheduled to be hosted in **Bhubaneswar, Odisha, in January 2025**.
 
• The Pravasi Bharatiya Divas Convention is celebrated biennially to strengthen the engagement of the Indian diaspora with their homeland.
 
• Bhubaneswar, the capital city of Odisha, has been chosen for its historical and cultural significance and its ability to host large-scale international events.
 
• Pravasi Bharatiya Divas marks the return of Mahatma Gandhi from South Africa to India on **9 January 1915**, symbolizing the contribution of the Indian diaspora to the nation's development.
 
• The event typically features discussions, cultural programs, and awards recognizing the contributions of Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Background of Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD):**

 
 
• The first Pravasi Bharatiya Divas was celebrated on **9 January 2003** in New Delhi.
 
• The event was conceptualized to acknowledge the contributions of the Indian diaspora in their respective fields worldwide.
 
• The Ministry of External Affairs organizes the event in collaboration with state governments and other stakeholders.

• To connect the Indian diaspora with the government and people of India.
 
• To discuss key issues related to NRIs and PIOs, including their role in India's socio-economic development.
 
• To honor exemplary contributions of overseas Indians through the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Awards.
 
 
 
• **Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Awards (PBSA):**
 
 
• PBSA is the highest honor conferred on NRIs, PIOs, or organizations/institutions run by them.
 
• The awards recognize their outstanding achievements in enhancing India's image globally or their contributions to Indian society.
